volumes.title: Number Systems and Math Foundations for DSA Interviews
volumes.subtitle: Part A: The Practical Numeric Foundation for Java Coding Interviews
volumes.volume_label: Learning Step 3 - Volume 1 of 18 - Part A of B
volumes.cover_deck: Build the numeric reasoning needed for digits, bases, overflow, divisibility, modular arithmetic, powers, roots, and bit-level interview prerequisites.
volumes.topic_line: DIGITS | BASES | OVERFLOW | MODULO | GCD | POWERS | JAVA
volumes.purpose: This volume closes the mathematical prerequisite gap before bit manipulation, arrays, binary search, hashing, and number-based coding problems. It is practical DSA mathematics, not an academic number-theory textbook.
prerequisites: Time and Space Complexity learning step
Willingness to dry-run arithmetic one digit at a time
recognition_signals: The input is a number or a numeric string
Digits, bases, divisibility, remainders, or cyclic indexes determine state
A mathematically correct expression may overflow a Java primitive
Repeated halving, doubling, powers, or roots explain the complexity
outcomes: Implement overflow-aware digit and base algorithms in Java
Choose among int, long, exact arithmetic, numeric strings, and BigInteger
Use divisibility, GCD, LCM, modulo, powers, and roots in interview problems
Explain the edge cases behind MIN_VALUE, negative remainder, shifts, and numeric parsing
practice_ladder: Foundation: trace digit extraction, reconstruction, and base conversion
Interview Core: implement reverse integer, GCD, large-number modulo, and string addition
SDE-2 Follow-up: define validation, overflow, and API contracts
Challenge: combine numeric strings, modulo state, and binary reasoning

volumes.title: Number Systems Interview Patterns and Rapid Revision
volumes.subtitle: Part B: Fifty-Two Implementations, Java Traps, Exercises, Solutions, and Readiness
volumes.volume_label: Learning Step 3 - Volume 1 of 18 - Part B of B
volumes.cover_deck: Convert the numeric foundation into reusable interview patterns, boundary-safe Java, debugging skill, timed practice, and rapid revision.
volumes.topic_line: 52 IMPLEMENTATIONS | JAVA TRAPS | DEBUGGING | SOLUTIONS | REVISION
volumes.purpose: This linked workbook completes Stage 1 with the 52-implementation catalog, Java number traps, conceptual and code-output questions, debugging tasks, coding exercises, solutions, follow-up chains, cheat sheet, and readiness assessment.
prerequisites: Ability to write and run small Java 21 methods
An error log for boundary, overflow, and contract mistakes
recognition_signals: A number concept is understood but implementation is not yet automatic
Boundary bugs appear during timed coding
The interviewer changes the range, sign, base, or overflow contract
Final revision needs retrieval and debugging rather than more passive reading
outcomes: Implement and explain all 52 mandatory number algorithms
Diagnose Java numeric traps from failing inputs
Complete short and medium problems under explicit contracts
Use the readiness assessment to decide when to advance to bit manipulation
practice_ladder: Foundation: retype the digit and conversion templates
Interview Core: solve the 52-implementation catalog by invariant
SDE-2 Follow-up: defend contracts, types, validation, and overflow behavior
Challenge: complete the mixed revision bank and follow-up chains under time

volumes.title: Time and Space Complexity for Java Interviews
volumes.subtitle: From First Operation Counts to SDE-2 Trade-off Reasoning
volumes.cover_deck: Build complexity intuition from zero, derive bounds from Java code, reason about memory and collections, then defend optimizations at SDE-2 depth.
volumes.topic_line: GROWTH | BIG-O | LOOPS | SPACE | COLLECTIONS | TRADE-OFFS
volumes.purpose: This volume is the bridge from Java syntax to algorithmic problem solving. It begins with concrete operation counts, introduces growth and space gently, then develops the qualified cost models, constraints, invariants, amortization, and optimization explanations expected in SDE-2 interviews.
prerequisites: Java Foundations Volume 03 through loops, methods, arrays, strings, and basic collections
Ability to dry-run short Java methods
No prior complexity notation is required
recognition_signals: A code snippet has loops, recursion, collection calls, copies, or generated output whose cost is unclear
Constraints may eliminate a brute-force solution
Nested work depends on aggregate pointer movement rather than visual nesting
A data-structure choice changes time, space, order, mutation, or guarantees
outcomes: Derive time, auxiliary space, and output space from Java code
Qualify best, worst, expected, amortized, and output-sensitive claims
Select Java collections using semantics and defensible cost models
Explain an optimization from baseline through invariant, proof, trade-off, and test evidence
practice_ladder: Foundation: count simple, sequential, logarithmic, and nested work
Interview Core: analyze two pointers, recursion, strings, copying, and collections
SDE-2 Follow-up: defend amortized, expected, output-sensitive, and ownership trade-offs
Challenge: complete the cumulative and final readiness assessments without notes

code_companion.title: Twenty-Four Executable Complexity Examples
code_companion.description: This dependency-free Java 21 companion validates behavior and operation counts for the volume's core growth shapes, space models, and collection choices. Compile with javac -Xlint:all -Werror ComplexityExamples.java and run with java ComplexityExamples. A successful run prints exactly PASS 24 complexity examples. Wall-clock timing is deliberately not used as proof of Big-O.

volumes.title: Java Foundations for Problem Solving
volumes.subtitle: Java Fundamentals for DSA and SDE-2 Interviews
volumes.cover_deck: Restart from the first Java program, master language and collection behavior, then prove interview readiness through executable examples, traps, debugging, and focused practice.
volumes.topic_line: JAVA BASICS | TYPES | OBJECTS | COLLECTIONS | TRAPS | INTERVIEWS
volumes.purpose: This volume is the canonical Java language foundation and the recommended first book in the series. It starts with source-to-execution and program structure, builds through types, control flow, methods, arrays, strings, objects, core libraries, exceptions, generics, and usage-first collections, then converts that knowledge into interview-quality implementation and debugging skill.
prerequisites: A Java 21 JDK is useful for running the examples
Curiosity and willingness to dry-run small programs
recognition_signals: A correct algorithm is failing because of Java semantics
Primitive, reference, equality, or pass-by-value behavior is unclear
Core List, Set, Map, Queue, Deque, or PriorityQueue usage is not automatic
The interviewer asks for cleaner, safer, or more testable Java
outcomes: Explain Java program execution and write compiling Java from the first program onward
Use types, control flow, methods, arrays, strings, objects, exceptions, generics, and core collections precisely
Diagnose common Java interview traps and write safe comparators and numeric expressions
Continue to Time and Space Complexity with enough Java fluency to analyze real code
practice_ladder: Foundation: trace types, expressions, methods, arrays, strings, objects, and collection operations
Interview Core: compile the 70-example companion and complete output/debugging drills
SDE-2 Follow-up: expose contracts, aliases, failure behavior, and collection trade-offs
Challenge: pass the cumulative and final readiness assessments without notes

code_companion.title: Seventy Compiling Java Fundamentals Examples
code_companion.description: This dependency-free Java 21 companion contains seventy executable checks spanning the mandatory fundamentals and core collection usage. Compile with javac -Xlint:all -Werror JavaFundamentalsExamples.java and run with java JavaFundamentalsExamples. A successful run prints exactly PASS 70 Java Fundamentals examples.

volumes.title: Bit Manipulation in Java
volumes.subtitle: From First Bits to SDE-2 Interview Techniques
volumes.cover_deck: Build bit intuition from zero, master Java masks and shifts, derive high-value interview shortcuts, and apply XOR, subset, trie, and packed-state patterns safely.
volumes.topic_line: BITS | MASKS | SHIFTS | XOR | SUBSETS | INTERVIEW SHORTCUTS
volumes.purpose: This dedicated volume turns the binary foundation from Volume 01 into a progressive Java interview toolkit. It begins with visible bit patterns and safe operators, derives each shortcut instead of asking readers to memorize it, then develops XOR families, subset state, SDE-2 problem patterns, Java APIs, and production-quality bit fields.
prerequisites: Java Foundations Volume 03 through operators, loops, arrays, and methods
Time and Space Complexity Volume 02 through logarithmic growth and output-sensitive analysis
Number Systems Volume 01 binary representation and two's-complement basics
recognition_signals: The state is a small bounded set of yes/no facts
The problem asks about powers of two, parity, set bits, or fixed-width representation
Duplicate counts allow XOR cancellation
Constraints make subset or submask state feasible
A repeated range-XOR or maximum-XOR query appears
outcomes: Trace Java int and long bit patterns, shifts, promotion, and sign behavior
Derive and implement safe test, set, clear, toggle, low-bit, count, power-of-two, and range-mask techniques
Select and prove XOR, prefix-XOR, subset, submask, range-AND, and maximum-XOR patterns
Choose among primitive masks, BitSet, EnumSet, boolean arrays, and sets
Explain complexity, contracts, edge cases, and SDE-2 follow-ups without relying on unexplained tricks
practice_ladder: Foundation: draw bit patterns and trace operators before coding
Interview Core: implement masks, bit counts, power tests, XOR families, and range queries
SDE-2 Follow-up: prove invariants, handle signed boundaries, and compare alternative representations
Challenge: solve submask, bitmask-state, maximum-XOR, and packed-field problems under time

code_companion.title: Forty Executable Bit-Manipulation Checks
code_companion.description: This dependency-free Java 21 companion turns the volume's core identities, XOR patterns, subset methods, range techniques, and packed-field contracts into forty executable checks. Compile with javac -Xlint:all -Werror BitManipulationExamples.java and run with java BitManipulationExamples. A successful run prints exactly PASS 40 Bit Manipulation checks.

volumes.title: Loop Mastery, Patterns, and Index Calculations
volumes.subtitle: From Your First Loop to SDE-2 Index Reasoning
volumes.cover_deck: See exactly how Java executes loops, eliminate off-by-one errors, and derive the pointer, window, search, and grid patterns expected in SDE-2 interviews.
volumes.topic_line: LOOP EXECUTION | RANGES | POINTERS | WINDOWS | SEARCH | GRIDS
volumes.purpose: This volume is the bridge from basic Java control flow to reliable array and string problem solving. It begins with the execution model of for, while, do-while, and enhanced-for loops; builds a visual language for ranges and invariants; then derives pointer, compaction, window, search, and matrix patterns without asking the reader to memorize templates blindly.
prerequisites: Java Foundations Volume 03 through conditions, methods, arrays, and basic collections
Time and Space Complexity Volume 02 through linear, quadratic, and aggregate work
Number Systems Volume 01 for integer range and overflow intuition
recognition_signals: An endpoint or empty input creates an off-by-one failure
Two indexes move under different conditions
A contiguous range can reuse state instead of recomputing it
A nested loop may have aggregate linear work
A matrix or flattened index needs safe row/column arithmetic
outcomes: Trace every Java loop form using condition, body, update, and exit state
Design half-open ranges, invariants, and progress measures before coding
Implement two pointers, compaction, windows, lower bound, and matrix traversals safely
Explain Java enhanced-for translation, bounds checks, iterators, mutation rules, overflow, and termination
Defend loop correctness, complexity, edge cases, and production contracts at SDE-2 depth
practice_ladder: Foundation: predict basic loop execution and repair bounds
Interview Core: implement pointers, compaction, windows, search, and grids
SDE-2 Follow-up: prove invariants, aggregate work, overflow safety, and API contracts
Challenge: complete cumulative assessments and the final readiness interview

code_companion.title: 40 Executable Loop Checks
code_companion.description: This dependency-free Java 21 companion validates loop execution, bounds, two-pointer movement, compaction, sliding windows, lower bounds, flattened indexes, and matrix traversals. Compile with javac --release 21 -Xlint:all -Werror LoopMasteryExamples.java and run with java LoopMasteryExamples. A successful run prints exactly PASS 40 Loop Mastery checks.
